newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan plays down row after army talks.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan plays down row after army talks.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on Tuesday played down a dispute with the military over religious activism after talks with armed forces chief Ismail Hakki Karadayi.

"As will be seen, the top ranks of the state are one, they are together. Our president, our government and our army are one body," Erbakan told reporters after an hour and 40 minutes of talks with the chief of staff.
Witnesses said Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist leader, welcomed the military chief at the main door of the prime minister's office.
Growing secularist pressure, led by the armed forces, on his coalition with conservatives is threatening the future of the 10-month-old alliance.

"He is coming to see me and I will hug him," Erbakan, known for his colourful rhetoric, earlier told a meeting of his Islam-based Welfare Party MPs. "The press will go crazy. I am saying this in advance so they don't have a heart attack."

The army and Erbakan's Islamist-led alliance have been at odds for the last two months over army demands for a crackdown on. A leading general said on Tuesday that the army's fight against an Islamist upsurge was a matter of life or death.
Erbakan has delayed implementing the military's anti-Islamist orders.
